name: mvolkov-skills
description: Claude Code plugin marketplace bundling best-practices skills for an async-first Python backend stack — SQLAlchemy 2.0, FastAPI, pytest, gRPC (grpc.aio), git workflow, OpenTelemetry observability, money / payments / ledger engineering — a Playwright-MCP-driven web QA skill (user flows, UX, Boy Scout mode) — plus two domain skills for interactive-gaming-platform work: GLI-19 platform certification readiness and GLI Gaming Security Framework (GLI-GSF) security engineering

plugins.name: sqlalchemy-best-practices
plugins.description: SQLAlchemy 2.0 async-first best practices — engine and pool config, Mapped[T] models, relationship loading strategies (selectin/select/write_only), query optimization, async sessions and transactions, FastAPI dependency injection

plugins.name: fastapi-best-practices
plugins.description: FastAPI production best practices — domain-organized project structure, async correctness (no blocking I/O, no CPU work in BackgroundTasks), DI patterns with per-request caching and chaining, Pydantic v2 split create/update/response models, Pydantic Settings v2 with .env and lru_cache, async testing with httpx.AsyncClient

plugins.name: pytest-best-practices
plugins.description: pytest async-first testing best practices — test layer structure (unit/integration/e2e), fixture design with proper scope, async testing with pytest-asyncio (asyncio_mode=auto), test data with factory_boy + faker, HTTP mocking with respx, time mocking with freezegun, property-based with hypothesis, DB transaction-rollback isolation, flush() pattern for chained DB fixtures, pytest-xdist parallelism

plugins.name: grpc-python-best-practices
plugins.description: Python gRPC async-first Kubernetes-native best practices using grpc.aio — server bootstrap with graceful shutdown that flips Health to NOT_SERVING before server.stop(), shared per-process channel factory, canonical decorator pattern (@grpc_logger + @grpc_error_handler) for cross-cutting concerns, max_connection_age_* triad for HPA rebalancing, client-side LB via dns:/// + round_robin + service config JSON over a Kubernetes headless Service (no service mesh), ERROR_MAP + google.rpc.Status rich error model, client-side translation hierarchy

plugins.name: git-workflow-best-practices
plugins.description: Git workflow best practices — Git Flow branch prefixes (feature/bugfix/hotfix/release), Conventional Commits format with feat/fix/docs/style/refactor/test/chore types, atomic commits with imperative mood, pre-commit hygiene (tests/diff/lint/no-debug/no-secrets), pull --rebase before push, no force-push to shared branches, max ~400 LOC per PR, self-review first, squash on merge for clean main history

plugins.name: observability-best-practices
plugins.description: Python observability best practices using OpenTelemetry — SDK bootstrap with off-switch contract and idempotency guard, auto-instrumentation (gRPC/SQLAlchemy/FastAPI/Logging), the LoggingInstrumentor + structlog correlation pattern with custom log hook and CleanLoggingHandler, two-tier log field taxonomy, span attribute conventions with <service>.<key> prefix for cross-service Tempo search, sensitive-field redaction at the serialization boundary, status taxonomy, metrics cardinality control, tail-based sampling, and Sentry-with-OTel integration

plugins.name: money-and-payments-best-practices
plugins.description: Engineering best practices for money / payments / ledger systems — Decimal or integer minor units (never float), the two-layer idempotency model (client-driven idempotency_key + chain-CAS for state transitions, never conflated), double-entry ledger architecture (Accounts + Transfers, debit=credit invariant at DB level, append-only, balance computed not stored), two-phase transfers via HOLD balance, atomic chains for composite operations, transaction state machines with optimistic concurrency control, external payment provider integration via stateless proxy + sync request + async webhook with three-layer dedup, reversibility via separate transaction with parent_transaction_id, and DB-enforced invariants

plugins.name: gli-19-platform-engineering
plugins.description: Engineering rules for an interactive (online) gaming platform that has to pass a GLI-19 technical certification — server-authoritative game outcomes with no game logic on the client, one authoritative system clock, the records a gaming system must maintain (per-game play record, per-theme aggregates with theoretical RTP, player-account record, significant-event log, operator-access record), append-only financial history with integrity hashing and actor attribution, supervised alteration of accounting data, restricted incentive credits wagered before unrestricted funds, game-cycle exclusivity and interrupted-game hold/completion, game recall, player-account lifecycle and MFA boundaries, most-restrictive limit precedence, payout-destination binding, geolocation checks, on-demand disable controls, regulator reporting surfaces, control-program verification, and communications / crypto / key-management obligations. 81 rules mapped to GLI-19 v3.0 requirement ids

plugins.name: gli-gsf-security
plugins.description: Security-engineering rules for an interactive gaming platform under the GLI Gaming Security Framework (GLI-GSF-1) — the deep security-controls layer beneath GLI-19's technical-security appendix, owning the infrastructure and network security it deferred. Logical access control and RBAC with separation of duties, authentication and ephemeral session authorization, secrets and key management with key agility, encryption of data at rest and in transit, network segmentation (production DBs isolated from patron-facing tiers), component hardening, DNS security, remote access and default-deny firewalls with no bypass path, tamper-evident security logging and monitoring, at-least-daily immutable backups and disaster recovery, secure SDLC and change management with release segregation of duties, and third-party-provider integration that cannot route into production. 72 rules mapped to GIS control ids with GIG1/GIG2/GIG3 assurance tiers

plugins.name: playwright-web-qa
plugins.description: Manual / exploratory web QA through the Playwright MCP browser tools — snapshot-first interaction, console + network inspection after every step, user-flow walking (happy / alternate / error / abandon-and-resume / first-time / per-role), functional heuristics per screen, accessibility via the accessibility tree, Nielsen-based UX evaluation with 0-4 severity, measured layout quality (alignment, spacing rhythm, form composition and field balance, typography), and Boy Scout mode that fixes everything found at the root and re-verifies until clean
